steps.tx: Start **enteral nutrition** within 24 to 48 hours in a patient who is resuscitated and has a working gut. The **gastric route** is first. **Post-pyloric feeding** is for intolerance or high aspiration risk, not the default. Early enteral nutrition maintains gut mucosal barrier integrity, prevents bacterial translocation, and dampens systemic inflammatory responses.

steps.tx: **CALORIES** found no mortality difference between the early parenteral route and the early enteral route. **NUTRIREA-2** found more bowel ischaemia with early full dose enteral feeding in shocked patients, without a mortality benefit. Enteral feeds must be held during escalating vasopressor therapy to avoid non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia.

Early full enteral vs parenteral in shock
Enteral arm caused significantly more acute mesenteric ischaemia
Withhold enteral nutrition during acute unresuscitated shock

steps.tx: **EDEN** found that **trophic enteral feeding** for the first 6 days was not inferior to full enteral feeding for ventilator free days. Full calories on day 1 are not mandatory. Delivering minimal trophic volume around 10 to 20 mL per hour preserves gut architecture while preventing hyperglycaemia, gastrointestinal distension, and metabolic stress.

points: Targeted full caloric prescription from day one

steps.tx: The **EFFORT Protein** trial found that a higher protein dose did not improve outcomes and may harm patients with **acute kidney injury** and high organ failure scores. More protein is not always better. Supplying protein in excess of 2.2 g/kg/day during acute illness exacerbates uraemic solute load and cellular organ failure.

More protein is not always better. Supplying protein in excess of 2 point 2 g/kg/day during acute illness exacerbates uraemic solute load and cellular organ failure.

rows: Poorer recovery and increased mortality in severe AKI
Better clinical trajectory in multiple organ dysfunction
Titrate protein moderately and avoid excessive early loads

steps.tx: **PERMIT** found that **permissive underfeeding** of calories, with protein maintained, did not change mortality compared with full calorie feeding. Providing 40% to 60% of calculated caloric needs alongside recommended protein intake achieves equivalent clinical outcomes, demonstrating that avoiding early overfeeding is safe in critical illness.

points: Maintained full recommended target protein dose

right.title: Targeted full feeding
points: Higher incidence of insulin requirement and hypercapnia
Confirmed hypocaloric feeding is clinically non-inferior

steps.tx: **EPaNIC** found that early **supplemental parenteral nutrition** increased infections compared with withholding it until day 8. Parenteral nutrition is not added on day 1 just to meet a calorie target. Allowing mild early macronutrient deficit promotes cellular autophagy and clears damaged organelles, protecting against nosocomial infection.

Increased hospital infections and delayed ICU discharge
Withheld until day 8 of ICU stay
Accelerated recovery and reduced new organ failure
Delay parenteral nutrition until second week if enteral fails

steps.tx: A single **gastric residual** below 500 mL is not a reason to stop feeds. **Prokinetics** are tried before the tube is declared a failure. Residual checks are not required by routine. Monitoring for abdominal distension and passage of flatus is safer than reflexively interrupting nutrition for moderate aspirated fluid volumes.

left.title: Gastric residual volume policy
points: Threshold up to 500 mL without vomiting is acceptable
Avoid routine hourly aspirate checks in stable patients
Prevents unwarranted interruption of nutritional delivery

right.title: Motility enhancement
points: Post-pyloric feeding if dysmotility persists despite drugs

steps.tx: **Refeeding risk** is highest in starved, alcoholic, and very underweight patients. Give **thiamine**, replace phosphate, potassium, and magnesium, and raise calories over several days. Cautious stepwise escalation of nutritional delivery over four to seven days prevents fatal cardiopulmonary decompensation and ventricular arrhythmias during metabolic recovery.
